title: Cohomology over an open etale object is cohomology on the open scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $j:U\to X$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on the small etale site $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. For every $q\geq0$, cohomology over the object $j:U\to X$ of $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] is canonically isomorphic to $H^q(U_{\mathrm{Et}},j^{-1}G)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], via the equivalence of the localized site $X_{\mathrm{Et}}/U$ with the small etale site $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$. The isomorphisms are natural in $G$ and in restriction along inclusions of open subschemes. If $G=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}$ for a quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent] and $\kappa_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*\mathcal F$ is the natural open-immersion pullback isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction], then $j^{-1}G$ identifies naturally with $(\mathcal F|_U)_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module].

proof.text: Because an open immersion $j:U\to X$ is etale, apply the localization equivalence to the object $j$ of $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$. A $U$-etale object $v:V\to U$ corresponds to $(j\circ v:V\to X, v:V\to U)$, and the two covering topologies coincide. This equivalence sends $\mathrm{id}_U$ to the final object of $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$.

source.place: Sites, Section 00XZ (section-localize), specialized to the etale site

proof.text: For every $v:V\to U$ in $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$, the restriction $G|_U$ of $G$ to $X_{\mathrm{Et}}/U$ has value $G(V\to U\to X)$. The etale inverse-image restriction theorem identifies $j^{-1}G(V)$ with this same group, using the original restriction maps of $G$. Thus the sheaf transported from the slice site by step 1 is $j^{-1}G$; the identification is natural in $G$ and remains compatible with a further open inclusion.

source.place: Sites, Section 00XZ (section-localize), and etale inverse-image restriction

proof.text: Apply Stacks 03F3(1) to the constant integer ring on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$: restriction of an injective abelian sheaf to $X_{\mathrm{Et}}/U$ remains injective, since it is right adjoint to exact extension by zero. In an injective resolution $G\to I^\bullet$, restriction therefore gives an injective resolution on the slice site, and $I^n(U)=(I^n|_U)(\mathrm{id}_U)$. Taking cohomology of these identical complexes gives $H^q(U,G)\cong H^q(\mathrm{id}_U,G|_U)$, naturally in $G$ and in restriction to smaller open objects.

Use the site equivalence of step 1 with $W=\mathrm{id}_U$ in the cohomology transport theorem: it identifies $H^q(\mathrm{id}_U,G|_U)$ with cohomology over the final object of $U_{\mathrm{Et}}$ for the transported sheaf. By step 2 that sheaf is $j^{-1}G$; evaluation at the final object is the global-sections functor $\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{Et}},-)$ [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor], and an injective resolution $j^{-1}G\to J^\bullet$ (bounded below, injective terms) is a K-injective resolution [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so this cohomology is $H^q(U_{\mathrm{Et}},j^{-1}G)$ as defined by K-injective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. The naturality in $G$ and further inclusions follows from the naturality of the three comparisons.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 03F3, and Sites, Section 00XZ

proof.text: Set $G=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{et}}$. For each etale $v:V\to U$, step 2 gives $(j^{-1}G)(V)=G(j\circ v)=\Gamma(V,(j\circ v)^*\mathcal F)$. Apply $c_{v,j}^{-1}$ to identify this with $\Gamma(V,v^*j^*\mathcal F)$ and then $v^*(\kappa_{\mathcal F}^{-1})$ to identify it with $\Gamma(V,v^*(\mathcal F|_U))=((\mathcal F|_U)_{\mathrm{et}})(V)$. Naturality of $c_{v,j}$ and $\kappa_{\mathcal F}$ makes these maps commute with each restriction $\rho_g$, whose formula and composition law are given by the etale quasi-coherent presheaf nodes. Thus the sectionwise maps form the stated natural isomorphism of sheaves.
